gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's US prices across the EcoFlow range. At us.ecoflow.com the 2,048 Wh DELTA 3 Max costs $879 (about $0.43/Wh), $150 less than the older 2,048 Wh DELTA 2 Max at $1,029, and the 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W DELTA 3 Classic costs $459, $120 less than the DELTA 3 at $579.
standout_why: I opened the solarkontor.de guide. It names 15 EcoFlow models but gives no prices, no capacity or output per model, and no value ranking; its country selector shows EUR, not US prices. I couldn't read the other rival pages today: shopsolarkits.com/collections/ecoflow returned HTTP 429 twice, tech.yahoo.com returned 403, trailandkale.com returned 404 and rei.com returned 403. The shopsolarkits collection is a store page and probably shows some prices, so I don't score this 3. The other pages are single-product reviews or launch news (DELTA Max, DELTA 3 Plus, Trail 300 DC, RIVER 3 Plus) and can't give a price across the whole range.
decides: The pick should go by price per Wh. For about 2 kWh, the DELTA 3 Max ($879) beats the DELTA 2 Max ($1,029): same 2,048 Wh, same 3,400 W X-Boost figure, $150 less. The DELTA 3 Max Plus ($1,149) costs $270 more than the DELTA 3 Max, for 3,000 W instead of 2,400 W and a 2–10 kWh expansion range. For 1 kWh, the DELTA 3 Classic ($459) beats the DELTA 3 ($579) on price. The DELTA 3 listing names 5 recharging methods, including the 800 W Alternator Charger and Smart Generator; the Classic listing says '4 Ways to Charge'. For about 3 kWh, the DELTA 3 Ultra ($1,299, $0.42/Wh) is the cheapest per Wh of everything I priced. It costs $300 less than the DELTA 3 Ultra Plus ($1,599), which adds 3–11 kWh expansion and 6 ways to charge. For a small portable unit, the RIVER 2 Pro (768 Wh, $369, $0.48/Wh) costs less per Wh than any other RIVER I could price. The DELTA Pro 3 ($2,799) is listed as unavailable until late January.
